judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad one-way indemnity covering 'any and all claims, demands or legal causes of action of any nature whatsoever (including without limitation legal expenses), arising out of or related to Recipient's acceptance, use and disposal of the Materials ... including but not limited to any and all claims for personal injury or death' is expansive but not internally uncertain; 'arising out of or related to' is the only elastic phrase. Its one-sidedness could attract contra proferentem, but only if some genuine ambiguity first appeared.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with paragraph 2 (sole responsibility for handling and use), paragraph 6's disclaimer and paragraph 8's insurance requirement, and it is expressly listed as surviving in paragraph 10. No contradicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause states 'Three Million ($1,000,000) dollars aggregate' — the words and the numeral disagree, a mechanical error that directly changes the required coverage; 'occurrence basis, or claims made including tail coverage' is also left to the Recipient's election without a standard. The words-versus-figures mismatch is a nameable defect on the face of the provision, even allowing for the document's poor scan quality.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the letter fixes coverage amounts; paragraph 9 merely requires a certificate confirming 'the insurance coverage set forth in section 8', so the internal error propagates but no other provision contradicts it. Insurance is also absent from the paragraph 10 survival list, which is a minor gap rather than an incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite obligation to furnish a certificate on request confirming section 8 coverage and promising thirty days' notice of cancellation or reduction; the only softness is that the insurer, not the Recipient, must make the promise. There is no term here whose meaning two parties would plausibly dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cross-reference to section 8 is accurate and section 8 exists; unlike paragraph 10's 'Sections 5, 5 and 7', this reference points somewhere unambiguous. No conflict with any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sections 5, 5 and 7 shall survive' is a mechanical error on the face of the clause — the same number is listed twice and section 6 (or the second paragraph numbered 5) is not clearly captured — so the survival of the ownership, publication-review and warranty-disclaimer terms is left uncertain. 'Breaches any term' with no materiality qualifier and the duty to 'return all Materials and progeny' also lack boundaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The MTA has no stated term or expiration yet the clause refers to 'termination or expiration', and the duplicate '5' can only be resolved by reading paragraphs 5 (ownership) and 5-bis (disclaimer) together, so the clause cannot be applied without construing the document's numbering as a whole. That is a specific incoherence traceable to paragraphs 5 and 6/5-bis.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard modification-in-writing, non-waiver and severability boilerplate, each sentence self-contained and definite; 'to the extent permitted by law' is conventional rather than ambiguous. Nothing here names a contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is unnumbered and hangs after paragraph 10, which is a formatting slip rather than a conflict, and nothing in paragraphs 1-10 or the closing letter contradicts the writing/waiver/severability regime. No inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing request to return a signed copy and the statement that 'The Materials will be forwarded to you upon receipt of the signed letter' are plain instructions; the only issue is whether they are formation conditions or mere logistics. That is a slim, unnamed ambiguity rather than a contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the preamble's 'Before receiving the materials, we ask that you and your Institute agree', and the signature block requires signature by Dr. June and an authorised institutional official, matching the collective 'Recipient' definition. No operative provision pulls the other way.
